Lines on the song's beats over the waveforms: bar starts strong, the other beats pale. Zoom in to see every beat.
Finds the song's chords in the background and shows their names in a row over the tracks. A click on a name corrects it.
A parametric equalizer for every stem: drag the five bands on the curve, set a bell's width with the wheel, switch it off to hear the difference. It changes only what you hear, never the files.
Play your part along with the song: pick the stem you play, mute it and record yourself. Your waveform runs under the original's, and after a take you see how many notes were on time.

Every note of the take, from its start to its end
On time within ±{tolerance} ms ({note} at {bpm} BPM, a beat being 1/4); early or late beyond it; missed: no note within 80 ms.
On time within ±{tolerance} ms; early or late beyond it; missed: no note within 80 ms.

Why ±15 ms by default: about 20 ms apart is the least at which the ear tells which of two notes came first, so notes within ±15 ms sound together with the original. A tighter value trains finer timing; a looser one suits a first go.
Hold one earcup against the pickup of your instrument (or the microphone), then press Start. Clicks play one at a time; the recorded ones move into line with the played ones.

Tune your guitar or bass by ear: a click on a string's note plays a steady tone of it until you click elsewhere or press Esc or Space. Standard, drop D, 7-string guitar and 5-string bass.
Zoom the waveforms with the mouse wheel or a trackpad pinch, around the pointer. Shift + wheel or a sideways swipe moves the view; while playing, the view follows the playhead.
